title: 交换机自学习与泛洪：MAC 地址表的演化
expected_output:
=== switch self-learning and forwarding ===
--- frame 1: AA(port1) -> BB(unknown) ---
  in=1  src=AA  dst=BB  [learned src -> port 1]
    action: FLOOD (unknown dst) -> [2, 3, 4]
    mac table: {'AA': 1}
--- frame 2: BB(port2) -> AA(known) ---
  in=2  src=BB  dst=AA  [learned src -> port 2]
    action: UNICAST -> port 1
    mac table: {'AA': 1, 'BB': 2}
--- frame 3: AA(port1) -> BB(known) ---
  in=1  src=AA  dst=BB
    action: UNICAST -> port 2
    mac table: {'AA': 1, 'BB': 2}
--- frame 4: CC(port1) -> broadcast ---
  in=1  src=CC  dst=FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF  [learned src -> port 1]
    action: FLOOD (broadcast) -> [2, 3, 4]
    mac table: {'AA': 1, 'BB': 2, 'CC': 1}
--- frame 5: AA(port3) moved! MAC migration ---
  in=3  src=AA  dst=BB
    action: UNICAST -> port 2
    mac table: {'AA': 3, 'BB': 2, 'CC': 1}

=== properties ===
  each port is its own COLLISION domain (full duplex, no CSMA/CD needed)
  broadcast frames still flood -> switch does NOT separate BROADCAST domains
  a router (or VLAN) is required to separate broadcast domains
  entries age out (default 300 s); MAC flooding attack overflows the table
code:
class Switch:
    def __init__(self, ports, name="SW1"):
        self.name, self.ports, self.table = name, ports, {}
        self.log = []
    def rx(self, src, dst, in_port):
        learned = src not in self.table
        self.table[src] = in_port
        if dst == "FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF":
            act = f"FLOOD (broadcast) -> {[p for p in self.ports if p != in_port]}"
        elif dst in self.table:
            out = self.table[dst]
            if out == in_port:
                act = f"FILTER (dst on same port {in_port})"
            else:
                act = f"UNICAST -> port {out}"
        else:
            act = f"FLOOD (unknown dst) -> {[p for p in self.ports if p != in_port]}"
        flag = "  [learned src -> port %d]" % in_port if learned else ""
        print(f"  in={in_port}  src={src}  dst={dst}{flag}")
        print(f"    action: {act}")
        print(f"    mac table: {dict(sorted(self.table.items()))}")
        self.log.append((src, dst, in_port, act))

print("=== switch self-learning and forwarding ===")
sw = Switch([1, 2, 3, 4])
print("--- frame 1: AA(port1) -> BB(unknown) ---")
sw.rx("AA", "BB", 1)
print("--- frame 2: BB(port2) -> AA(known) ---")
sw.rx("BB", "AA", 2)
print("--- frame 3: AA(port1) -> BB(known) ---")
sw.rx("AA", "BB", 1)
print("--- frame 4: CC(port1) -> broadcast ---")
sw.rx("CC", "FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF", 1)
print("--- frame 5: AA(port3) moved! MAC migration ---")
sw.rx("AA", "BB", 3)
print()
print("=== properties ===")
print("  each port is its own COLLISION domain (full duplex, no CSMA/CD needed)")
print("  broadcast frames still flood -> switch does NOT separate BROADCAST domains")
print("  a router (or VLAN) is required to separate broadcast domains")
print("  entries age out (default 300 s); MAC flooding attack overflows the table")
